Definition: a border of a river (as cut into by the stream)
BiblicalUsage: Gadah is the bank of a river, the edge where the water cuts into the land. The river of Assyria shall come up over all his channels and go over all his banks in Isaiah 8:7, and the Jordan overflowed all his banks all the time of harvest when the priests' feet touched the water in Joshua 3:15. The waters returned to their place and flowed over all his banks when the ark came up in Joshua 4:18, and the men who crossed in the first month put to flight all the valleys in 1 Chronicles 12:15.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the overflowing banks are a picture of God's power breaking its bounds. The Jordan was full, yet the priests walked through on dry ground, and I hold that no flood is too full for God to part.
